newsitem.title: UK: BP says weather delays Foinaven oil again.
newsitem.headline: BP says weather delays Foinaven oil again.

text.p: Production at British Petroleum Plc (BP)'s troubled Foinaven oil field west of the Shetland Islands has been delayed again, an official said on Tuesday.
An Aberdeen-based official said first oil was still "a few weeks" away with work on the final testing and commissioning of the subsea infrastructure still to be completed.
"We've got force eight gales and eight metre seas which makes it damn difficult to get on with the work," he said.
Foinaven, the first field to be developed in the waters of the Atlantic margin, was originally due on stream in June 1996 but a series of technical mishaps have delayed the project by almost a year.

The field, discovered some five years ago by operator BP in partnership with Royal/Dutch Shell, has estimated recoverable reserves of 250 million barrels and should reach peak output of 120,000 barrels per day (bpd).
BP and Shell have made two other commercial finds on the Atlantic margin, Schiehallion due to start pumping by mid-1998, and more recently Suilven.
Output from Britain's newest oil province is expected to more than compensate for declining output in established areas of the North Sea.
Last month, the Department of Trade and Industry awarded 14 operators 25 permits to explore for oil, mainly in marginal waters west of the Hebrides and north of the Shetlands.
Norwegian offshore services group Awilco ASA said in early April it had completed the final tie-in of the Petrojarl production vessel at Foinaven.
Awilco will continue to receive an undisclosed dayrate from BP to cover direct costs until the subsea system is ready.
